2. Petitioner's father and 13 others took Pattan of 14 Anna share of Kamraghop Beel Fishery situated at SA Plot No. 1448 by a registered pattani patta dated 2nd Kartick 1358 BS corresponding to 31-12-1950 from the 14 annas landlords of the same and remaining 2 Anna share of the said fishery belonging to other landlords was settled with one Inamullah, one of the persons who took pattan of the 14 Anna share thereof, for 30 years with affect from 1359 BS by a registered lease deed dated 6th Kartick 1359 BS and thus the petitioner after his father's death and his co-sharers have been in possession of the said fishery in leasehold right. In case No. 92 of 1958 on 1-4-1958 the said fishery was leased out to Abdur Rahman and Darbesh Ali by the Government. Thereafter petitioner and his co-sharers as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 180 of 1958 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Habigonj against the Government and those lessees for declaration and the said suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiffs on 11-4-1960. Government preferred Title Appeal No. 306 of 1960 against the said judgment and decree and the said appeal was dismissed on 31-5-1961. Thereafter Government filed Second Appeal No.1167 of 1962 and by order dated 5-5-76 the said appeal abated as a whole. Petitioner contends that during pendency of the said suit said fishery was wrongly recorded in the Khas Khatian No. 1 in SA Plot No. 1448 in correctly recording the area of the fishery as .38 acres instead of 65.38 acres and they claimed that in spite of such record they continued in possession. When respondent No. 3 again leased out the said fishery to one Rajendra Kumar for 3 years from 1396 to 1398 BS petitioner filed an application before the respondent No. 2 against the said order praying for cancellation of the lease granted to the said Rajendra Kumar and the same was registered as Misc. Case No. 1 of 1989. Respondent No. 2 by order dated 26-12-89 disallowed the case filed by the petitioner. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Petitioner's main contention is that no compensation assessment roll was prepared in his name in respect of his pattani or raiyoti interest in the disputed fishery and, as such, his interest did not vest in the Government and he is entitled to possess the same till final publication of such compensation assessment roll.
